active.currentEndpoint: All prose presently contained in the surviving Google working draft has been committed through Chapter X. Chapter VII establishes the physical hull wound and Meren Holt's repeated hesitation; Chapter VIII establishes Kelm's protective attachment to the Hesperant Vale, the eleven-hour high-risk versus 36–54 hour slow repair choice, Kelm's six-second helm-failure account and the approximately fourteen-second telemetry absence; Chapter IX establishes the crew's demonstrated integrity, Sella Varn, Torren, and repair progress; Chapter X names the missing forward-hold inspection team as Jerrik Noll, Edren Vale and Pallas Dorn and ends with Broussard ordering the search. Conversation-history review found no additional post-X prose: only earlier variants of the same missing-team/loose-bin setup. The deep-index telemetry falsification, predator battle, successful convoy return and reader-only Genestealer reveal remain authorial continuity for future new prose, not recovered source text.
active.nextSlice: No source-recovery backlog remains in the observed Google working draft. When this story next becomes rotation-eligible for new prose, begin immediately after “Let’s go find them,” preserve the established missing-team search plan and character-state ledger, and build toward the authorial continuity constraints without prematurely granting Broussard or Jalesthesian reader-only knowledge.
constraints: Fourteen-second telemetry gap is a surface anomaly, not the main plot hole.
Deep-indexed older telemetry was falsified to conceal the freighter's true port of origin.
Hesperant Vale crew is secretly compromised by Genestealer influence.
Genestealer hybrids are hidden among loose produce bins in the forward holds.
Broussard's detachment successfully returns the damaged freighter to the convoy after fighting additional High Presidio predators.
The reader sees the hidden Xenos travesty continuing beneath the apparent successful rescue.
Recover Google source sequentially and verbatim before fresh expansion.
